agree.reason: The candid tone, the real factory quote and the honest note on the 8.1 rating will reassure this wary backer, but there is no budget breakdown and no delivery date, so someone who once lost $85 may still hold back.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the 'proven hit' claim and qualifies the small sample, but 'We're closer than it looks' oversells things, since a 46% conversion from a sign-up list would be unusually high.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 572 backers needed and the 46% of sign-ups, but it never adds $17,400 to roughly $5,150 in backer shipping to show the remaining margin, and it never addresses printing 1,500 copies against 572 backers.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison is backers needed against sign-ups, given in its most hopeful form with no realistic conversion rate, and there is nothing on how this campaign compares with first-time projects that fail to ship.

qualification.reason: It names the $28,000 threshold and says what happens if the goal is missed, but it gives no fulfilment date and no checkable milestone, and it has no risks section of the kind this reader looks for.

objections.reason: It raises the first-time creator worry openly and answers it with the quote, the shipping figure and the testing record, but it leaves the reader's obvious questions about timeline, fees and cost overruns unanswered.

fit.reason: It is a pitch of about 500 words with clear crowdfunding sections, though it reasonably declines the brief's request to call the game a proven hit.
